faq: Do you only work with real estate?
Yes. Agents, teams, brokerages, developers and property managers. Working in one industry lets us start faster and get the details right, from signage sizes to brokerage co-branding rules.
Is BeBrand a real estate brokerage?
No. BeBrand is a digital agency. We do not list, sell or manage property. We design the brand, the marketing and the website for the people who do.
What does it cost?

One-off projects start at $1,999 and monthly plans at $699; every price is in the pricing section. Anything beyond what a package lists is quoted as a fixed price before work starts, so there are no hourly surprises.
How does onboarding work?
It is two short steps online: who you are, then what you need, with your budget and timeline. We reply by email, and a kickoff call comes next.
How long does a project take?
It depends on scope. A personal brand kit is quick; a full firm identity with a website takes longer. You get a timeline in writing before we start, and we keep to it.
Can you work within my brokerage's brand rules?
Yes. Most agent brands have to sit beside a brokerage logo and follow its guidelines. We design for that from the first sketch. Send us the rules when we start.
What do I receive at the end?
All final files in print and screen formats, the editable source files, your brand guidelines, font licenses and the logins for anything we set up for you.
Can I mix services from different packages?
Yes. During onboarding you can tick any of the seven services, whichever package you start from.
I'm a new agent. Is it too early for a brand?
No. A clear personal brand helps most at the start, when you have fewer closed deals to point to. The personal brand kit is built for exactly this stage.
Do you build the website as well?
Yes. We design it, show it to you as a live prototype, then build it with listings, lead capture and a CMS you can update yourself.
Who will I be working with?
The designers you meet on the first call. Nothing is handed down to someone you have never spoken to.
